name: 2 Timothy

overview.author: The apostle Paul (1:1), writing his final letter.
overview.date: About AD 64–67, from a Roman prison shortly before his execution under Nero.
overview.audience: Timothy, Paul’s beloved son in the faith, still ministering in Ephesus.
overview.setting: Paul is in chains, deserted by many, expecting death. False teaching and persecution threatened the churches.
overview.purpose: To urge Timothy to be unashamed of the gospel, suffer as a good soldier, guard and preach the word, and come to Paul quickly.
overview.structure: Be unashamed and guard the gospel (1), endure as a soldier, athlete, and farmer (2), know Scripture amid godless times (3), and preach the word as Paul finishes his race (4).

items.title: Godlessness and the sufficiency of Scripture

themes.title: Unashamed Faith
themes.text: Do not be ashamed of the testimony about the Lord or of Paul.

themes.title: Guarding the Gospel
themes.text: Guard the good deposit by the Holy Spirit.

themes.title: Passing It On
themes.text: Entrust the truth to faithful people who will teach others.

themes.title: Endurance in Suffering
themes.text: Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

themes.title: The Word of God
themes.text: All Scripture is breathed out by God and equips us.

themes.title: Faithful to the End
themes.text: Paul has fought the good fight and finished the race.

christInBook.text: Christ Jesus abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, the offspring of David.
If we die with Him, we will live with Him; if we are faithless, He remains faithful.
The Lord, the righteous judge, will award the crown of righteousness.

reflection: What gift has God given you that may need to be fanned into flame (1:6)?
Who are you investing in so they can pass the faith on (2:2)?
What does it look like to rightly handle the word of truth (2:15)?
How is Scripture equipping you for good works right now (3:16–17)?
How do you want to be able to describe your life at the end, as Paul does in 4:7?

chapterList.title: Not Ashamed of the Gospel
chapterList.summary: Paul thanks God for Timothy’s sincere faith, which first lived in his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice. “Fan into flame the gift of God.” God gave a spirit of power, love, and self-control, not fear. Do not be ashamed; share in suffering. Christ abolished death. Paul is not ashamed, for he knows whom he has believed. Guard the good deposit. Onesiphorus was not ashamed of Paul’s chains.
questions: How did faith pass down to Timothy (1:5)?
What does God’s Spirit give instead of fear (1:7)?

chapterList.title: A Good Soldier of Christ
chapterList.summary: Be strengthened by grace and entrust the gospel to faithful people who will teach others. Share in suffering like a soldier, compete by the rules like an athlete, work hard like a farmer. Remember Jesus Christ, risen. If we are faithless, He remains faithful. Rightly handle the word of truth. Flee youthful passions; pursue righteousness. The Lord’s servant must be kind and patiently correct opponents.
questions: What do the soldier, athlete, and farmer teach about ministry (2:3–6)?
How should we correct those who oppose the truth (2:24–26)?

chapterList.title: The Sufficiency of Scripture
chapterList.summary: In the last days people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, proud, and lovers of pleasure rather than God, having a form of godliness but denying its power. Timothy has followed Paul’s teaching and sufferings. All who desire to live godly lives will be persecuted. “All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness.”
questions: Which traits of the last days do you see in our culture (3:1–5)?
Why should godly people expect persecution (3:12)?
What does 3:16–17 teach about the Bible?

chapterList.title: Finish the Race
chapterList.summary: Paul solemnly charges Timothy: “Preach the word; be ready in season and out of season.” People will gather teachers to suit their passions. Do the work of an evangelist. Paul is being poured out as a drink offering: “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.” Many deserted him, but the Lord stood by him. He asks Timothy to come quickly and bring Mark.
questions: What does it mean to preach “in season and out of season” (4:2)?
Why do people seek teachers who tell them what they want (4:3–4)?
How does Paul face death with confidence (4:6–8)?

tagline: Guard the gospel, endure hardship, and finish the race
readingPlan: 4 chapters: one chapter a day takes 4 days; two a day takes about 2 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
